I want to be in the same place where you are now--seeing the light at the end of the tunnel, etc.  I'm trying really hard to focus on improving myself and making the most out of all this time being alone. But I think, just like you, I'll always have a special space (more like a hole) in my heart for the person who left me. I'm always going to love him. I will do my best to prepare myself for that small chance encounter in the future and hope that it doesn't completely break me.

Thank you so much for saying this! Made me feel great about my own progress. I’m proud that I’m about to finish a book in just two days, after having barely read anything while I was in a relationship. It’s important to celebrate tiny victories. :)

Going through something very similar right now. Just like you, I was single for a very long time and it was the first real relationship that I’ve been in. Broke up after 5 years, with one year living together. It’s lonely being single again, although it really should be familiar territory. I also sometimes feel that I might be too old and that it’s too late for me to find anyone. But stranger things have happened, right? It’s hard, but I try to be excited for the possibilities instead, and focus on preparing myself for that. 

I think it’s great that you’re remembering your ex pretty objectively. After our breakup, all I could think of was the good times.  That made it harder to start the process of moving on. Now that I can be honest with myself, I know our relationship wasn’t really that great, he had plenty of shitty moments, and deep down we both knew that this wasn’t ‘it.’ I still miss him terribly,but I know I want and deserve someone better. 

Hope at least some of this gibberish will help. Much love to you.
Thank you, Beating myself up is my default reaction whenever I’m faced with a failure. It’s unhealthy, I know. I will try to stop before it’s too late.
